editorNote: A quiet day for launches: a contested claim about editing model weights, a Pentium-era chess thought experiment, and several small tools and guides.

stories.headline: A 'Weight-Space Programming' post says a frontier model can read and edit network weights; a rebuttal says the framing misleads
stories.summary: The post says GPT-6 Astra raised Qwen3.5-0.8B's MATH-500 score from 7.9% to 48.1% by editing about 0.016% of weights, mostly by stopping reasoning loops. Honnibal replies that the Qwen result uses Python and practice batches rather than raw-weight reading, and that one game comparison is weaker than the abstract suggests.
stories.whyItMatters: It separates what was shown (edits that unlock existing ability in one small model) from the broader claim; the authors themselves say Gemma 3 270M did not benefit.

sourceLinks.title: Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen
The 'Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen' post is misleading

stories.headline: Carlini ports Stockfish to a 1996 Pentium Pro and estimates it would have beaten Kasparov
stories.summary: On a 200 MHz Pentium Pro with 64 MB of RAM, a tuned Stockfish 17 port scored about 3109 Elo at 10 seconds per move, which the author extrapolates to roughly 3300 at classical time controls. It beat the original 1996 Crafty 78 to 5, with 17 draws.
stories.whyItMatters: The author attributes about 720 of the 1,335 Elo gained since 1996 to software rather than hardware.

sourceLinks.title: Could a modern chess engine on a Pentium have defeated Kasparov in 1996?

stories.headline: Subvocal, a YC F26 startup, shows glasses that turn silently mouthed words into text
stories.summary: The glasses emit low-power radio waves and decode changes in how mouthing modulates them, via cloud models with latency usually under 500 ms. The company is taking preorders for 500 units and expects to ship in Q1 2027.
stories.whyItMatters: Commenters' main objection was sending internal speech to the cloud; the founders say they hope to support local inference later.

sourceLinks.title: Show HN: Subvocal – Talk to your computer without making noise

stories.headline: Nvidia open-sources Auto Ontology, a context layer that lets agents query enterprise data
stories.summary: The Apache-2.0 library builds ontologies from metadata, reconciles metric definitions, and turns natural-language questions into SQL for Databricks, Postgres, Snowflake or DuckDB. It exposes this via MCP, CLI and API.
stories.whyItMatters: The README warns that without the optional Vault, credentials added through the UI are stored in plaintext in Postgres, and the project is not accepting outside contributions.

stories.headline: ERICI launches a non-commercial effort to build an open software stack for RISC-V industrial computers
stories.summary: Started by Yuri Zaporozhets in Ravensburg, Germany, the initiative defines interfaces from firmware to operating systems and calls a box that boots the stack on RVA23 hardware ERICI-compatible. It says it sells nothing and charges no fees.
stories.whyItMatters: The page says RVA23 silicon now exists but open, partitioned software for industrial RISC-V machines does not; it states no funding sources.

stories.headline: NIST publishes a plain-language cybersecurity guide for one-person businesses
stories.summary: White Paper 50, released Nov. 2, selects actions from CSF 2.0 such as regular backups, software updates and changing default passwords, with worksheets and three example solopreneurs. It updates NISTIR 7621.
stories.whyItMatters: Non-employer firms get a guide written for people with no security background.

sourceLinks.title: Self-Employed? Solopreneur? NIST Has a Cybersecurity Guide Just for You
